correctness.rationale: The module decomposition bijection and centralizer unit quotient yield a fully normalized integer Gaussian-binomial formula. The first positive coefficient has q-adic scale q^{2d(B-1)} times a strictly increasing finite q^{-1} sum in [1,q), recovering B and m_d. At each j, the shorter-block contribution is computable solely from previously recovered multiplicities and B; the remaining coefficient is zero or a strictly increasing known-prefactor geometric sum recovering m_j. This proves the inverse theorem for every nilpotent dimension and every prime-power q. Exhaustive direct matrix checks and 22-dimensional partition inversion tests corroborate calculations, but are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: A finite-field matrix rank polynomial of natural commuting algebraic projections is a complete similarity invariant on all nilpotent matrices, with a constructive explicit coefficient algorithm even without pre-specified dimension. This is a structural inverse theorem rather than a routine restatement of the classical forward count: a coarse univariate projection-rank distribution unexpectedly recovers every Jordan block length and multiplicity. It is reusable for invariant recognition and cannot be obtained by merely reading a single count or centralizer dimension.
